clusters.name: LEARN PYTHON
clusters.heading: Learn Python by building, not by watching tutorials.
clusters.body: Most ways to learn Python lead through tutorials: type this into the console, copy that into a notebook, repeat. Useful for a week. At 42 Belgium, learning Python happens differently. The Common Core treats Python as a working tool: you write scripts that solve real problems, you debug your own code, you read other people's code in peer reviews. Coding Python well isn't about syntax — it's about thinking in functions, knowing when to use a list versus a generator, building things that don't break in three months. You can learn Python free elsewhere — YouTube, Coursera, freeCodeCamp. What you can't get there is the engineering rhythm: real projects, peer feedback, code review, and a campus full of people learning Python alongside you.

clusters.name: PYTHON CERTIFICATION
clusters.heading: Python certification: what 42 actually offers.
clusters.body: 42 Belgium doesn't issue a Python certification of its own — Python is a tool inside the broader curriculum, not a separate course you pass with a stamp. If you came looking for a Python certification specifically, the honest answer is: most aren't worth as much as the work they signal. What 42 offers is different: a Python course inside the full Common Core, where the work itself becomes evidence. For formal European recognition, the RNCP 6 framework gives you a professional diploma at bachelor level — earned by passing the broader curriculum, not by typing through a 40-question multiple choice. If you want a vendor certification (PCEP, PCAP), the Python work here prepares you to pass them on the side.

faq.question: Is this a standalone Python course?
faq.answer: No — Python at 42 Belgium is part of the Common Core curriculum, not a course you sign up for separately. You start with C in your first weeks, then Python comes in alongside algorithms, systems and data work. By the time you've shipped a few projects, Python is no longer a "language you're learning" — it's a tool you use.

faq.question: How long until I can actually code in Python?
faq.answer: A few weeks. The Common Core takes 12 to 18 months end-to-end, but Python work starts early. The deeper question is when you can build production-ready Python: that's a function of how many projects you ship, which depends on you.

faq.question: Will I get a Python certification?
faq.answer: Not directly from 42. We don't issue Python-specific certifications — the curriculum produces engineers, not certificate-holders. If you complete the broader curriculum, the RNCP 6 framework gives you a professional diploma recognised across Europe at bachelor level. For vendor certifications like PCEP or PCAP, the Python work here prepares you to take them on your own.
